```{r}

library(BiocManager)
library(phyloseq)
library(Biostrings)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyverse)
library(tibble)
library(microViz)
library(microbiome)
library(ggpubr)
library(patchwork)
```

# Prepare the Phyloseq Object

### Remember, Phyloseq is picky with formatting!

#### Format:

- OTU (or ASV) Count Table: Matrix

- Taxonomy Table: Matrix

  - Note that Domain in this column in this data is actually the database used to annotate the ASV.

- Sample Data (or Metadata) Table: Data Frame

#### A helpful graphic from [Holmes and McMurdie (2013)](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0061217) for remembering this structure: 

![Figure 3 from the PLOS One paper](images/PS_structure.png){fig-align="center"}

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| label: read-data
#| code-fold: true
#| eval: true
#| output: false
#| code-summary: "Code to read in and format data for Phyloseq"

Pt_taxa <- as.data.frame(read.csv("Pt_microbiome_taxa.csv", row.names = 1))
Pt_counts <- as.data.frame(read.csv("Pt_microbiome_counts.csv", row.names = 1))
Pt_meta <- as.data.frame(read.csv("Pt_microbiome_metadata.csv", row.names = 1))

dim(Pt_taxa)
dim(Pt_counts)
dim(Pt_meta)

head(Pt_taxa)
head(Pt_counts)
head(Pt_meta)

#Set count table rownames to ASVs
taxa <- rownames(Pt_counts)
taxa_ASV_names <- taxa %>% str_replace_all("sp", "ASV")
rownames(Pt_counts) <- taxa_ASV_names #This has to be the same as the taxonomy table
rownames(Pt_taxa) <- rownames(Pt_counts)

samples <- rownames(Pt_meta)
Pt_meta$"Sample" <- samples
if (all(colnames(Pt_counts) == samples)) {
  print("Good to go")
} else {
  print("The count and metadata tables do not have equal sample data")
}
colnames(Pt_counts) <- Pt_meta$Sample 
```

- The OTU table column names have to equal the sample data rownames.

  - If taxa are rows in the OTU table.

### Now let's build the Phyloseq object with the taxonomy, OTU, and metadata tables.

- You can also add a phylogenetic tree and fasta sequences to the object, but we won't cover that here.

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| label: build-phyloseq-object
#| code-fold: true
#| output: false
#| code-summary: "Code to check the classes of the Phyloseq object files and building the object"

if (class(Pt_taxa) == "data.frame") {
  Pt_taxa_mat <- as.matrix(Pt_taxa)
} else{
  print("Not a data frame")
}

if (class(Pt_counts) == "data.frame") {
  Pt_counts_mat <- as.matrix(Pt_counts)
} else{
  print("Not a data frame")
}

if (class(Pt_meta) == "data.frame") {
  print("Good to go!")
} else{
  print("You need a data frame")
}

Pt_Microbiome_PS <- phyloseq(otu_table(Pt_counts_mat, taxa_are_rows = TRUE), 
                             tax_table(Pt_taxa_mat), 
                             sam_data(Pt_meta))
Pt_Microbiome_PS
```

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| label: examining-object
#| code-fold: true
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
#| code-summary: "Code to examine Phyloseq object contents"

Pt_Microbiome_PS@otu_table
Pt_Microbiome_PS@tax_table
Pt_Microbiome_PS@sam_data
Pt_Microbiome_PS@refseq
Pt_Microbiome_PS@phy_tree

#You could re-save these contents as files like this: 

Pt_Microbiome_PS_taxa <- data.frame(Pt_Microbiome_PS@tax_table)
head(Pt_Microbiome_PS_taxa)
class(Pt_Microbiome_PS_taxa)
```

# Phyloseq Microbiome Analysis

### Preparing the Phyloseq object for analyses

- Do you spot any issues with the present taxa?

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| label: cleaning-object

#Check for contaminant species
Pt_Microbiome_PS_sp <- Pt_Microbiome_PS %>% 
  microbiome::aggregate_taxa(level = "Species")
Pt_Microbiome_PS_sp

Species_DF <- data.frame(Pt_Microbiome_PS_sp@tax_table)
sort(unique(Species_DF$Species)) #Easier to look at this in the console

unwanted_species <- c("Escherichia coli", "Pt Chloroplast", "Unassigned")

Pt_Microbiome_PS_sp_clean <- Pt_Microbiome_PS_sp %>% 
  subset_taxa(!Species %in% unwanted_species) #Trim away these taxa we don't want
Pt_Microbiome_PS_sp_clean

#Since this is qSIP data, we don't want to merge all the density bins into their original source tubes (each from one single culture)--biological replicates in Iron-Replete and Iron-Deplete cultures (13C/12C-bicarbonate added to cultures count as additional replicates).
Pt_Microbiome_PS_Culture <- Pt_Microbiome_PS_sp_clean %>% 
  merge_samples("Source", fun = "sum")
Pt_Microbiome_PS_Culture

#For some reason, this screws up some of the variables, so let's add them back

Sample <- rownames(Pt_Microbiome_PS_Culture@sam_data) #This variable will be corrected later on
dput(Sample) #Copy this to easily fill in new variables manually
Iron <- c("High", "High", "High", "High", "High", "High", 
          "Low", "Low", "Low", "Low", "Low", "Low")

sample_data(Pt_Microbiome_PS_Culture)$Iron <- Iron
sample_data(Pt_Microbiome_PS_Culture)$Iron #Check that it worked

#Now let's rarefy the object and remove very low-count taxa
sort(sample_sums(Pt_Microbiome_PS_sp_clean))
sort(sample_sums(Pt_Microbiome_PS_Culture))
mindepth <- min(sample_sums(Pt_Microbiome_PS_Culture))
Pt_Microbiome_PS_Culture_Rare <- Pt_Microbiome_PS_Culture %>% 
  rarefy_even_depth(sample.size = mindepth, replace = FALSE)

sort(sample_sums(Pt_Microbiome_PS_Culture_Rare))
sort(taxa_sums(Pt_Microbiome_PS_Culture_Rare))

Pt_Microbiome_PS_Culture_Rare <- prune_taxa(taxa_sums(Pt_Microbiome_PS_Culture_Rare) > 100,
                                            Pt_Microbiome_PS_Culture_Rare)

sort(taxa_sums(Pt_Microbiome_PS_Culture_Rare))
```

### Now let's do some alpha- and beta-diversity exploring with MicroViz

- The code for MicroViz plots generated in the GUI can be copied, pasted, and modified in RStudio!

```{r}
#| eval: false

Pt_Microbiome_PS_Culture_Rare %>% tax_fix() %>% ord_explore()

```

### Some example alpha-div. plots using the MicroViz and Microbiome packages

```{r}
#| label: making-figures
#| warning: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Making alpha-div. figures"
#| fig-cap-location: bottom
#| fig-cap: "Alpha diversity measurements of the *P. tricornutum* enrichment community without the inclusion of chloroplast sequences, colored by Iron availability. A. is Shannon diversity and B. is inverse Simpson diversity—each showing richness and evenness of heterotroph species."
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-alt: "Two dot plots of alpha-diversity across culture replicates"

#Diversity (applies to sam_data)
Pt_Microbiome_Div_DF <- Pt_Microbiome_PS_Culture_Rare %>% 
  microbiome::diversity(index = "all")

Pt_Meta_PS <- data.frame(Pt_Microbiome_PS_Culture_Rare@sam_data)
Pt_Meta_PS_Div <- cbind(Pt_Meta_PS, Pt_Microbiome_Div_DF) %>% 
  dplyr::select(-Sample) %>% 
  rownames_to_column("Sample")

Shanplot <- Pt_Meta_PS_Div %>% ggplot(aes(x = Sample, y = shannon)) +
  geom_point(size = 4, shape = 21, color = "black", aes(fill = Iron)) + 
  theme_classic2() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("purple", "darkgreen")) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(2, 2.5), 
                     breaks = c(2.1, 2.2, 2.3, 2.4, 2.5)) +
  labs(y = "Shannon Diversity", x = "") +
  theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 12, color = "black"), 
        legend.text = element_text(size = 12, color = "black"))

Simpplot <- Pt_Meta_PS_Div %>% ggplot(aes(x = Sample, y = inverse_simpson)) +
  geom_point(size = 4, shape = 21, color = "black", aes(fill = Iron)) + 
  theme_classic2() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("purple", "darkgreen")) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(6.2, 8.4), 
                     breaks = seq(6.2, 8.4, by = 0.4)) +
  labs(y = "Inv. Simpson Diversity", x = "") +
  theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 12, color = "black"), 
        legend.text = element_text(size = 12, color = "black"))

(Shanplot + Simpplot) +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") + #Add one shared legend
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A", tag_suffix = ".") #Control your caption labels
```
